title: The Empty Plate on Monday
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Every Monday, I keep a voluntary fast, a habit I picked up almost two years ago after a difficult season made me want something steady to hold onto.
Narrator: I've never announced it at work, partly because I dislike being asked questions I'd rather not turn into a whole conversation over lunch.
Narrator: [carefully] The trouble is, my team has a standing Monday tradition of ordering food together, and my empty plate has started drawing more attention than I'd like.
Narrator: Last week, a new colleague asked, loudly enough for half the table to hear, whether I was on some kind of diet, and something about the question made me flinch.
Narrator: [reflective] I could have simply said yes, diet, and let the conversation end there without any further explanation required of me.
Narrator: Instead, almost without deciding to, I told the truth, that I was fasting, though I kept the explanation as brief as I possibly could manage.
Narrator: [honestly] Predictably, that opened a small flood of questions, why, how often, whether it was difficult, none of them unkind, but all of them more attention than I wanted.
Narrator: Afterward, I found myself wishing I'd simply said nothing was wrong and let them assume I wasn't hungry that particular day.

Narrator: [gently] What unsettled me wasn't the questions themselves, but noticing how badly I wanted the whole table to see me as disciplined, rather than simply fasting quietly like any other Monday.
Narrator: That single flicker of wanting to be admired for it told me more about my own heart than the fast itself ever has.
Narrator: [calmly] So this week, when someone glanced at my plate again, I only said I wasn't very hungry, and let the conversation move somewhere else entirely.
Narrator: It felt like a small, almost invisible correction, choosing plainness over the version of the story that would have made me look good.
Narrator: [encouraging] The fasting itself hasn't changed at all; what changed is how carefully I'm trying to keep it between myself and the only audience that ever mattered.

quiz.question: What habit has the narrator kept for almost two years?
options: A voluntary fast every Monday
A daily gym routine
A weekly journal
A strict diet plan
quiz.explanation: Every Monday, he keeps a voluntary fast, a habit he picked up almost two years ago.

quiz.question: What makes keeping it private difficult at work?
options: His manager requires medical records
He works from home
He has no coworkers
His team has a standing Monday tradition of ordering food together
quiz.explanation: His team's standing Monday tradition of ordering food together makes his empty plate draw attention.

quiz.question: What happened last week at lunch?
options: A new colleague loudly asked if he was on a diet
He was fired for not eating
He fainted from hunger
His manager praised his discipline
quiz.explanation: A new colleague asked, loudly enough for half the table to hear, whether he was on some kind of diet.

quiz.question: What unsettled the narrator most after explaining he was fasting?
options: That people didn't believe him
That he broke his fast accidentally
Noticing how badly he wanted to be seen as disciplined rather than just fasting quietly
That his coworkers stopped inviting him to lunch
quiz.explanation: He was unsettled by noticing his own desire to be admired for the fast rather than simply doing it quietly.

quiz.question: What did he do differently the following week?
options: He said he wasn't very hungry and let the conversation move on
He skipped the lunch entirely
He announced his fasting schedule to the whole team
He asked to stop the lunch tradition
quiz.explanation: When someone glanced at his plate again, he only said he wasn't very hungry, choosing plainness over drawing attention.

quiz.question: Why does the Monday lunch tradition complicate the narrator's private fast?
options: Updates listed quantities received and remaining needs rather than faces.
His empty plate repeatedly attracts questions from colleagues.
The team should remove that person's image from the material.
They should ask why and listen before choosing another method.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: His empty plate repeatedly attracts questions from colleagues.

quiz.question: What reaction reveals a problem in his intention after he explains the fast?
options: They feared less personal information would weaken accountability.
Aid must not depend on revealing identity, diagnosis, or hardship.
The voucher may be unusable, while landlord contact could create risk.
He notices that he wants colleagues to admire his discipline.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He notices that he wants colleagues to admire his discipline.

quiz.question: How does he answer a similar question the following Monday?
options: Financial reports, receipts, inventory counts, and independent review.
Use only necessary details covered by specific consent.
He simply says he is not very hungry and changes the subject.
They should have meaningful input whenever circumstances allow.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He simply says he is not very hungry and changes the subject.

quiz.question: Why does he prefer the less impressive explanation?
options: More recipients collected support directly and volunteers heard fewer rumours.
Plainness protects the fast from becoming a source of praise.
Audited figures, clear procedures, and responsible reporting.
Thanks for aid is not informed consent to publish hardship.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Plainness protects the fast from becoming a source of praise.

quiz.question: What remains unchanged despite his new way of answering coworkers?
options: It must not take their privacy, voice, or right to receive help quietly.
Crowding does not replace guardian permission and appropriate safeguards.
Use an established emergency process with verification, privacy, and records.
He continues the voluntary Monday fast.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He continues the voluntary Monday fast.
